shared_elements: upright boulder-shaped stone monument with rounded/tapering top
shallow low-relief carving on a weathered, pitted surface
frontal standing human figure occupying the central axis
broad headdress or head-covering filling the upper zone
arms/hands rendered as low relief with held or flanking objects
small block-like glyph or panel motifs
horizontal band of repeated pattern crossing the lower portion
justification: Both stones share a strikingly similar overall scheme: a tall rounded slab whose entire face is filled by a single frontal figure, headdress or crown across the top, arms and held elements at mid-height, and a horizontal band of repeated motifs low on the shaft, all in shallow, eroded relief. The clearest difference is in the mid-field: A centres a large concentric disc on the chest with sweeping curved bands, whereas B fills the flanks with vertical columns of small rectangular glyph-like blocks and a much busier, more legible basal band.
